messages:
Priya (ML Eng): quick sync — ran a small bring-up for Lumen (≈7B) with the new int6 quant profile overnight. 2k mixed-turn chat slices across support+search-rewrite slices. short recap + recs below.
Alex (Prod): nice — high level numbers?
Priya (ML Eng): perf first: median token latency ~48ms, p95 ~210ms (tokens/sec ≈400). cost/token estimate ~0.0009 USD vs baseline fp16 ~0.0016 — ~44% savings. quality: +1.8% EM on retrieval-qa slice, but hallucination rate up ~0.7% on multi-turn followups (mainly shorter prompt contexts).
Samir (Research): what's the slice composition and sample size? any priming sensitivity?
Priya (ML Eng): slice = 60% single-turn QA (open-domain + retrieval), 30% multi-turn customer support dialogs, 10% instruction rewrite. total ≈2,000 examples (stratified). priming sensitivity: we saw degradation concentrated where system prompt included long context >2k tokens — KV cache pressure + quant rounding seems to amplify small prompt perturbations.
Marta (SRE): any memory / OOM issues on the runners?
Priya (ML Eng): no OOMs. Peak GPU mem per worker ~24.8GB on A10G equivalent. kv-cache hit rates unchanged vs int8 baseline. throughput stable.
Alex (Prod): for product flows, what's safe to flip to int6?
Priya (ML Eng): recommendation split: route low-risk / high-volume endpoints (search summarization, internal tooling, ephemeral chat) -> int6; keep high-risk / user-facing verification flows (KYC, legal drafting, clinical triage) -> int8/fp16 until more regression fixes. Suggest canary at 10% traffic with automated quality gates (see thresholds).
Samir (Research): what gates? give exact numbers we can automate.
Priya (ML Eng): propose: EM on retrieval QA >= baseline - 0.5% (absolute), hallucination delta <= +0.5% (absolute), avg token-latency <= baseline *1.2. if any gate fails, rollback. Also monitor prompt-length bucketed drift.
Priya (ML Eng): quick ops snippet for rollout (route config excerpt):
```yaml
routes:
  - name: lumen-int6-lowrisk
    match: endpoint in ["/search", "/summarize"]
    variant: lumen-7b-int6
    traffic: 0.10  # start canary
    gates:
      quality_metric: retrieval_em
      min_delta: -0.005
      max_hallucination_delta: 0.005
```
Alex (Prod): can we compress further with prefix caching to recover some hallucination regressions?
Priya (ML Eng): yes — early experiments show prefix/KV caching of warm prompts reduces hallucination noise on multi-turn by ~0.3% (likely because fewer quantization-induced rounding transitions). we should enable prefix caching for chat sessions where user history >1 turn.
Marta (SRE): ml-ops-bot created a canary job: job id lumen-int6-canary-18654321. Will that run on dedicated pool or shared?
ml-ops-bot: Canary deployed to dedicated pool (tag: canary-medium). Runs: 10k tokens/day, telemetry -> /redwood/telemetry/lumen-int6-canary-18654321.
Samir (Research): any qualitative failure modes? examples?
Priya (ML Eng): shared a tiny sample in thread: most failures are subtle truncation or token-repetition on multi-question prompts. example: user asks follow-up clarifying question and model repeats earlier answer fragment — looks like softened attention distribution after quant rounding.
Alex (Prod): concrete next steps?
Priya (ML Eng): 1) start 10% canary for low-risk routes with the YAML above. 2) enable prefix caching for multi-turn chat for canary buckets. 3) run 24h focused regression check on the hallucination metric; if >+0.5% rollback. 4) schedule small sweep on numerics (int6 vs int8) for long-context prompts (2k-8k) next week. 5) compile a short scorecard for GTN with unit-econ table (we'll push to gdrive).
Marta (SRE): ack, I'll wire the telemetry alert (pager if hallucination delta > 1% in 1h).
Priya (ML Eng): thanks — will post the canary result summary in #eng-ml tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
